analysis.purpose: Initializes each 0x60-byte record’s threshold, retrieves three nullable candidates, and orders the final pair by floating-point differences. Their exact game meaning remains uncertain.
analysis.observed_abi: Receives an owner pointer in a0. The caller ignores the result and no consistent return-value setup is observed; C uses void without establishing the original return type. Each lookup receives a loaded global word in a0, a four-byte key in a1 also homed at sp+4, base record field_00+0xDC in a2, and zero in a3. Results are nullable pointers in v0.

evidence: Immutable expected bytes equal the original assembly. Both C builds reproduce all 440 bytes; the assigned fallback is absent.

Owner +0x44 is the record pointer and +0x48 the signed count. Records have stride 0x60, root pointer +0x00, float threshold +0x0C, and candidate pointers +0x4C/+0x54/+0x58. Candidate +0x64 and root +0xE4 are floats.
Bootup relocation sites 0x217C8/0x217FC/0x2182C resolve through Sym275 to func_05314C, corresponding to gl_func_0003EAE0.
Source sites 0xD114/0xD11C reference Sym274, named D_007770. Key-load pairs reference Sym2, the module Data base. Alias equations preserve these identities and pass the strict gate.
A named Data pointer prevents address hoisting. Declaring it before the keys places their stack slots at the original sp+0x68/0x64/0x60 offsets.
Normal and NON_MATCHING comparisons show no other function-byte changes or previously exact regressions.
Complete ROM equals baserom with MD5 fa27089c425dbab99f19245c5c997613. All six compressed-block checks pass.
